entries.title: My folk are idle (standing around)
q: why are my villagers not working
entries.answer: Folk keep hours: they rest at night (dusk to dawn), take a break at noon, keep a weekly day of rest, and go to festivals. Outside those, an idle folk usually lacks something: the tool of its trade, materials in the stores for its building, food (a hungry folk can't work properly), or work in its trade (more hands than the trade needs).
steps: Check the time: it's work from the dawn bell (6:00) to the dusk bell (18:00), less the noon break.
Ask it 'Your work today?' (Chat → More chat) or 'How are you?': it says what it's doing or missing.
Press J: what the town is short of. Look at its Profile → Day (plan vs what it's really doing).
Feed the town (food in the stores), supply what its trade lacks, or sell the town materials.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Chat → More chat → Your work today?
tips: Idle hands help the builders and bake bread, and the elder moves spare hands to trades that need them.
A folk with a red warning on its name tag is stuck: it digs or climbs its way out by itself.

entries.title: Nobody buys from my shop
q: customers dont come to my shop
why do folk say too dear
entries.answer: Folk buy only what they have a real use for now, at a price they think fair. Check four things: is the shop open (every checklist line ticked, within its hours)? Are its wares things folk here want (the Stock tab says who would buy each and why)? Are prices near the going price? Is its name good (fair prices, full shelves, a keeper who greets)?
steps: Open the shop → Shop tab: 'Getting started' shows what's missing, the next step first.
Stock & prices: read 'N of its wares have buyers in town' and 'Folk here want: ...'; stock those.
Press Going price on dear wares; 'too dear' turnings-down are on the Books tab.
Wait for hours: four customers a day at worst, two dozen at best; market day brings more.
warn: Worn tools don't sell; and nobody pays more than the town asks for something it has itself.

entries.title: My town isn't growing
q: why is my village not growing
how do i make my village bigger
entries.answer: Children come only with room and food: a free bed (houses keep up with births) and a day's meals for everybody in the stores, from two fed folk in work. So look at the larder, the homes and the mood; and the server's growth cap may stop a town past a size.
steps: Open the town's books → Overview: food, homes and beds, and what needs attention.
Food short? Help the farms: bring food, deliver Wanted orders; the elder orders 'Fill the larder'.
Homes short? Builders need materials: bring planks, stone, glass.
Raise contentment: a thriving town needs less food put by and has children more readily.
controls: Town's books → Overview · People → Growth · Homes
warn: villageGrowthCap (100) and the world cap stop children past them: ask your server's operator.

entries.title: Nothing is getting built
q: why isnt my village building anything
why is the building taking so long
entries.answer: Builders lay only what the stores really hold, so a shortage means a wait: the building's status says what it's waiting for ('waiting for 10 glass panes'). Some works also wait for an age, a hand the town can spare, or the town's own buildings first.
steps: Check what it waits for: the town's books → Town → Buildings, or your order on the property office's Orders tab.
Bring the material: sell it at the store, deliver it as a Wanted order, or give it to your order.
Paid orders get hands while fewer than half the town's grown folk are at its works.

entries.title: I can't found a town
q: why cant i found a town
entries.answer: The founding screen says why Confirm won't go. Usually: the server only lets citizens or operators found; you've founded the most towns a player may (3 by default); you carry no Founding Kit, spawner or charter; or the spot is too near a town, in water, or out of reach.
steps: Read the line under Confirm on the founding screen.
No kit? Craft one: 2 bread, wheat seeds, planks and a gold nugget.
Citizens only? Become a citizen of a town first ('May I live here?').
Pick another spot if this one is refused.

entries.title: The town won't make me a citizen
q: why cant i become a citizen
they wont let me live here
entries.answer: 'We hardly know you yet' means you're not a Friend of the village yet: the folk who know you must think well enough of you on average. 'Not while you owe a fine' means pay it. Otherwise it's 20 coins (unless the town built you a house).
steps: Talk to many folk daily; give presents; do errands.
Pay fines (Town → The watch → Pay a fine).
Carry 20 coins and ask 'Live here?' again.

entries.title: The town won't charter my business
q: why cant i start a business
only a citizen or friend may hold a charter
say hello to the nearest folk
entries.answer: The town charters anybody it knows and has nothing against: a citizen, a friend, or a visitor who has passed the time of day with its folk. A stranger nobody has spoken to is told so on step 1 with a 'Say hello' button; an unwelcome player must mend fences first. A shop of your own wants no standing at all.
steps: Press 'Say hello to the nearest folk' on step 1 (or talk to a few folk).
Or open a shop instead: U → Open a shop.

entries.title: Folk are leaving my town
q: why are folk leaving my village
entries.answer: After three miserable days (contentment under 25) somebody leaves, one every other day at most and never below eight. Folk also move for work a Wanted notice offers elsewhere, or when unhappy. Lift contentment: food, homes, wages paid, safety, things to enjoy, a day of rest.
steps: Check the town's books → Overview: contentment and its parts.
Talk round one thinking of leaving: 'Won't you stay?'.

entries.title: My town is stuck in an age
q: my town is stuck in the stone age
why wont my village reach the iron age
not enough iron for the next age
how do i help my town advance
entries.answer: Each age asks for things in the stores and buildings standing. Press J for what the town is short of, then help: deliver the Wanted orders, sell it iron or stone, take its quests, or bring its errands ('Can I help?' asks for what the next age needs).
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Ask → Can I help?

entries.title: My items disappeared in town
q: lost my loot when i died in town
entries.answer: Things left lying in a town's streets for two minutes are swept into the Lost and Found chest by the storehouse, kept for you alone for three days. Ask the storekeeper 'Lost & found' or right-click the chest.

entries.title: The folk don't like me
q: why dont the folk like me
entries.answer: Something cost you: hitting a folk, a theft or broken building seen by a witness, a fine unpaid, a quest given up, a bribe found out, or hated gifts. Say sorry (once a day each), pay what you owe, give liked presents, and let grudges fade; an outcast who stays away long enough can come back.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Chat → More chat → I'm sorry
Town → The watch → Pay a fine

entries.title: The town's books are empty
q: the town's books are written each morning
entries.answer: Most of the town's books are written each morning, so a brand-new town's pages fill in from its first day on. Overview, Folk, Society, Leader and News have today's figures already.

entries.title: My business is in trouble
entries.answer: A player's new firm has a week's grace. If it owes more than it's worth or runs out of cash and credit, you're told once a day in chat, and Your businesses says what's wrong, what to do (coin in its till on the Money tab, stock, a hand) and how many days are left before creditors may take it to court.

entries.title: Nobody's near enough to ask
q: ask the nearest folk does nothing
u page button says find a folk
entries.answer: Buttons that say 'Ask the nearest folk' speak to a grown, awake folk within about twelve blocks. Walk up to one (not a sleeping folk or a child) and press it again.

entries.title: The game is slow near a big town
entries.answer: Every folk is a ticking creature and drawn with its own animations, so hundreds are heavy. Found smaller towns; on your side, turn down how much of the folk's life is drawn (the client animation config) and name tags (K → Name tags). Operators can cap growth and let far towns sleep.

entries.title: My town is hungry
q: not enough food in the village
entries.answer: A hungry town orders the larder filled: half as many farmers and fishers again, wider fields, and in a famine twice the farmers and bread bought from traders. You can help by bringing food (gift it to the stores via errands, Wanted orders, or selling at the café and store).
